text:
Secret handshakes. Hidden rituals. Ancient mysteries. Political conspiracies. If you spend enough time online, you’ll eventually hear someone claim that the Freemasons are behind almost everything.

So…what is Freemasonry?

Like many subjects in history, Freemasonry has accumulated centuries of rumor, speculation, conspiracy theories, and exaggeration. The reality is both more interesting and, in many ways, less sensational than the legends.

Modern Freemasonry emerged in Britain during the late seventeenth and early eighteenth centuries, with the first Grand Lodge being organized in London in 1717. Freemasons themselves preserve traditions that symbolically connect their fraternity with the medieval stonemasons and even the builders of Solomon’s Temple. Historians, however, generally regard those connections as part of the fraternity’s traditional heritage rather than documented institutional history.

Mainstream, or “regular,” Freemasonry is a fraternity for men that seeks to encourage moral character, charity, fellowship, and personal improvement through symbolic ceremonies. Its lessons make extensive use of the tools of ancient stonemasons, such as the square and compasses, as moral illustrations. Freemasonry does not present itself as a church or claim to offer salvation.

Membership is generally limited to adult men who profess belief in a Supreme Being, although specific qualifications vary among Grand Lodges. The three foundational degrees are Entered Apprentice, Fellow Craft, and Master Mason. Other bodies, including the Scottish Rite and York Rite, offer additional instruction. The famous Thirty-third Degree is not a higher rank over all Freemasons but an honorary distinction within the Scottish Rite.

Because many of its ceremonies remain private, Freemasonry has attracted endless speculation. Over the centuries it has been accused of everything from controlling governments to preserving hidden religious knowledge. While individual Freemasons have certainly occupied influential positions throughout history, there is no credible evidence that Freemasonry operates as one unified organization directing world events.

Religion has often viewed Freemasonry with suspicion.

The Roman Catholic Church has consistently opposed Freemasonry since 1738, teaching that its principles are incompatible with Catholic doctrine. Today the Church teaches that Catholics who join Masonic associations place themselves in a state of grave sin and should not receive Holy Communion unless they have repented and been reconciled through the Church.

Several Eastern Orthodox Churches have likewise condemned or discouraged membership, although there has never been a single worldwide Orthodox position. Within the Anglican Communion and Protestantism more broadly, opinions have varied from acceptance to strong opposition.

Many well-known historical figures were Freemasons, including George Washington, Benjamin Franklin, Paul Revere, James Monroe, Andrew Jackson, Joseph Smith, Harry S. Truman, Winston Churchill, Giuseppe Garibaldi, and King George VI.

Whether someone ultimately views Freemasonry positively or negatively will usually depend upon their religious convictions and their reading of history. Whatever conclusion you reach, it is always better to understand something as it actually is than to rely solely on rumor, fear, or internet mythology.

Somaliland is a fascinating story in why sovereignty is so important. 

Politically, culturally, and geographically separate from Somaila - yet tied to Mogadishu thanks to a fundamentally flawed mid-century European understanding of African political landscapes - Somaliland’s unique political culture relies heavily on clan elder oversight and open democratic discourse. While neighboring nations like Djibouti and Ethiopia struggle under the weight of Chinese debt-trap diplomacy and the resulting erosion of their political autonomy, Somaliland stood its ground.

In the wide open, Somaliland, who have been self-governing while still being unwillingly tied to Somalia, chose to retain ties to Taiwan, rather than cut ties for a quarter of a billion dollars.

But here lies the geopolitical tragedy: Somaliland lacks formal international recognition. Under international law, it is still treated as part of Somalia - a state whose federal government maintains close ties to Beijing.

Predictably, Mogadishu used its internationally recognized legal authority to retaliate. By expanding an Air Defense Identification Zone over Somaliland's airspace, banning Taiwanese and Israeli passports, and implementing strict e-visa requirements, Somalia weaponized bureaucratic power to choke off air traffic and foreign investment into Somaliland's capital. While land borders with Ethiopia offer a temporary workaround, Somalia effectively used Beijing’s backing to strangle Somaliland economically... simply because a self-governing enclave refused to abandon an ally.

Ultimately, denying Somaliland formal statehood is no longer an exercise in maintaining regional stability - it is a tacit punishment of democratic success. For over three decades, Somaliland has met every textbook requirement of statehood, while rejecting the easy temptations of authoritarian bribes and foreign coercion. If international law exists to encourage peace, democratic governance, and the rule of law, then refusing to recognize a nation that embodies all three simply to appease a ghost union from 1960 renders those global principles meaningless. Somaliland has earned its sovereignty; the world just needs the courage to map it.

Venezuela as a state? Interesting

Funny side note, in the 1840s, the US had a chance to annex the Yucatan in Mexico.

About the same time the Republic of Texas declared independence from Mexico, so too did the Republic of the Yucatan. They even sent envoys to Washington expressing their desire to be annexed. The US passed on the offer.

Mexico, of course lost Texas, but was able to crush the Yucatec rebellion and reclaim the peninsula.

Otherwise, Cancun, Tulum, Merida, etc., would be American today.

text:
PROTOCOL No. 15

1. When we at last definitely come into our kingdom by the aid of COUPS D'ETAT prepared everywhere for one and the same day, after definitely acknowledged (and not a little time will pass before that comes about, perhaps even a whole century) we shall make it our task to see that against us such things as plots shall no longer exist. With this purpose we shall slay without mercy all who take arms (in hand, like Waco? Randy Weaver? Port Arthur? Oklahoma?) to oppose our coming into our kingdom. Every kind of new institution of anything like a secret society will also be punished with death; those of them which are now in existence, are known to us, serve us and have served us, we shall disband and send into exile to continents far removed from Europe. IN THIS WAY WE SHALL PROCEED WITH THOSE "GOY" MASONS WHO KNOW TOO MUCH; such of these as we may for some reason spare will be kept in constant fear of exile. We shall promulgate a law making all former members of secret societies liable to exile from Europe as the center of rule.

2. Resolutions of our government will be final, without appeal.

3. In the GOY societies, in which we have planted and deeply rooted discord and protestantism, the only possible way of restoring order is to employ merciless measures that prove the direct force of authority: no regard must be paid to the victims who fall, they suffer for the well-being of the future. The attainment of that well-being, even at the expense of sacrifices, is the duty of any kind of government that acknowledges as justification for its existence not only its privileges but its obligations. The principal guarantee of stability of rule is to confirm the aureole of power, and this aureole is attained only by such a majestic inflexibility of might as shall carry on its face the emblems of inviolability from mystical causes - from the choice of God. SUCH WAS, UNTIL RECENT TIMES, THE RUSSIAN AUTOCRACY, THE ONE AND ONLY SERIOUS FOE WE HAD IN THE WORLD, WITHOUT COUNTING THE PAPACY. Bear in mind the example when Italy, drenched with blood, never touched a hair of the head of Sulla who had poured forth that blood: Sulla enjoyed an apotheosis for his might in him, but his intrepid return to Italy ringed him round with inviolability. The people do not lay a finger on him who hypnotizes them by his daring and strength of mind.

SECRET SOCIETIES

4. Meantime, however, until we come into our kingdom, we shall act in the contrary way: we shall create and multiply free masonic lodges in all the countries of the world, absorb into them all who may become or who are prominent in public activity, for these lodges we shall find our principal intelligence office and means of influence. All these lodges we shall bring under one central administration, known to us alone and to all others absolutely unknown, which will be composed of our learned elders. The lodges will have their representatives who will serve to screen the above-mentioned administration of MASONRY and from whom will issue the watchword and program. In these lodges we shall tie together the knot which binds together all revolutionary and liberal elements. Their composition will be made up of all strata of society. The most secret political plots will be known to us and fall under our guiding hands on the very day of their conception. AMONG THE MEMBERS OF THESE LODGES WILL BE ALMOST ALL THE AGENTS OF INTERNATIONAL AND NATIONAL POLICE since their service is for us irreplaceable in the respect that the police is in a position not only to use its own particular measures with the insubordinate, but also to screen our activities and provide pretexts for discontents, ET CETERA.

5. The class of people who most willingly enter into secret societies are those who live by their wits, careerists, and in general people, mostly light-minded, with whom we shall have no difficulty in dealing and in using to wind up the mechanism of the machine devised by us. If this world grows agitated the meaning of that will be that we have had to stir up in order to break up its too great solidarity. BUT IF THERE SHOULD ARISE IN ITS MIDST A PLOT, THEN AT THE HEAD OF THAT PLOT WILL BE NO OTHER THAN ONE OF OUR MOST TRUSTED SERVANTS. It is natural that we and no other should lead MASONIC activities, for we know whither we are leading, we know the final goal of every form of activity whereas the GOYIM have knowledge of nothing, not even of the immediate effect of action; they put before themselves, usually, the momentary reckoning of the satisfaction of their self-opinion in
the accomplishment of their thought without even remarking that the very conception never belonged to their initiative but to our instigation of their thought ...

GENTILES ARE STUPID

6. The GOYIM enter the lodges out of curiosity or in the hope by their means to get a nibble at the public pie, and some of them in order to obtain a hearing before the public for their impracticable and groundless fantasies: they thirst for the emotion of success and applause, of which we are remarkably generous. And the reason why we give them this success is to make use of the high conceit of themselves to which it gives birth, for that insensibly disposes them to assimulate our suggestions without being on their guard against them in the fullness of their confidence that it is their own infallibility which is giving utterance to their own thoughts and that it is impossible for them to borrow those of others .... You cannot imagine to what extent the wisest of the GOYIM can be brought to a state of unconscious naivete in the presence of this condition of high conceit of themselves, and at the same time how easy it is to take the heart out of them by the slightest ill-success, though it be nothing more than the stoppage of the applause they had, and to reduce them to a slavish submission for the sake of winning a renewal of success .... BY SO MUCH AS OURS DISREGARD SUCCESS IF ONLY THEY CAN CARRY THROUGH THEIR PLANS, BY SO MUCH THE "GOYIM" ARE WILLING TO SACRIFICE ANY PLANS ONLY TO HAVE SUCCESS. This psychology of theirs materially facilitates for us the task of setting them in the required direction. These tigers in appearance have the souls of sheep and the wind blows freely through their heads. We have set them on the hobby-horse of an idea about the absorption of individuality by the symbolic unit of COLLECTIVISM .... They have never yet and they never will have the sense to reflect that this hobby-horse is a manifest violation of the most important law of nature, which has established from the very creation of the world one unit unlike another and precisely for the purpose of instituting individuality ....

7. If we have been able to bring them to such a pitch of stupid blindness is it not a proof, and an amazingly clear proof, of the degree to which the mind of the GOYIM is undeveloped in comparison with our mind? This it is, mainly, which guarantees our success.

GENTILES ARE CATTLE

8. And how far-seeing were our learned elders in ancient times when they said that to attain a serious end it behooves not to stop at any means or to count the victims sacrificed for the sake of that end .... We have not counted the victims of the seed of the GOY cattle, though we have sacrificed many of our own, but for that we have now already given them such a position on the earth as they could not even have dreamed of. The comparatively small numbers of the victims from the number of ours have preserved our nationality from destruction.

9. Death is the inevitable end for all. It is better to bring that end nearer to those who hinder our affairs than to ourselves, to the founders of this affair. WE EXECUTE MASONS IN SUCH WISE THAT NONE SAVE THE BROTHERHOOD CAN EVER HAVE A SUSPICION OF IT, NOT EVEN THE VICTIMS THEMSELVES OF OUR DEATH SENTENCE, THEY ALL DIE WHEN REQUIRED AS IF FROM A NORMAL KIND OF ILLNESS ..... Knowing this, even the brotherhood in its turn dare not protest. By such methods we have plucked out of the midst of MASONRY the very root of protest against our disposition. While preaching liberalism to the GOY we at the same time keep our own people and our agents in a state of unquestioning submission.

10. Under our influence the execution of the laws of the GOYIM has been reduced to a minimum. The prestige of the law has been exploded by the liberal interpretations introduced into this sphere. In the most important and fundamental affairs and questions, JUDGES DECIDE AS WE DICTATE TO THEM, see matters in the light wherewith we enfold them for the administration of the GOYIM, of course, through persons who are our tools though we do not appear to have anything in common with them - by newspaper opinion or by other means .... Even senators and the higher administration accept our counsels. The purely brute mind of the GOYIM is incapable of use for analysis and observation, and still more for the foreseeing whither a certain manner of setting a question may tend.

11. In this difference in capacity for thought between the GOYIM and ourselves may be clearly discerned the seal of our position as the Chosen People and of our higher quality of humanness, in contradistinction to the brute mind of the GOYIM. Their eyes are open, but see nothing before them and do not invent (unless perhaps, material things). From this it is plain that nature herself has destined us to guide and rule the world.

WE DEMAND SUBMISSION

12. When comes the time of our overt rule, the time to manifest its blessing, we shall remake all legislatures, all our laws will be brief, plain, stable, without any kind of interpretations, so that anyone will be in a position to know them perfectly. The main feature which will run right through them is submission to orders, and this principle will be carried to a grandiose height. Every abuse will then disappear in consequence of the responsibility of all down to the lowest unit before the higher authority of the representative of power. Abuses of power subordinate to this last instance will be so mercilessly punished that none will be found anxious to try experiments with their own powers. We shall follow up jealously every action of the administration on which depends the smooth running of the machinery of the State, for slackness in this produces slackness everywhere; not a single case of illegality or abuse of power will be left without exemplary punishment.

13. Concealment of guilt, connivance between those in the service of the administration - all this kind of evil will disappear after the very first examples of severe punishment. The aureole of our power demands suitable, that is, cruel, punishments for the slightest infringement, for the sake of gain, of its supreme prestige. The sufferer, though his punishment may exceed his fault, will count as a soldier falling on the administrative field of battle in the interests of authority, principle and law, which do not permit that any of those who hold the reins of the public coach should turn aside from the public highway to their own private paths. FOR EXAMPLES OUR JUDGES WILL KNOW THAT WHENEVER THEY FEEL DISPOSED TO PLUME THEMSELVES ON FOOLISH CLEMENCY THEY ARE VIOLATING THE LAW OF JUSTICE WHICH IS INSTITUTED FOR THE EXEMPLARY EDIFICATION OF MEN BY PENALTIES FOR LAPSES AND NOT FOR DISPLAY OF THE SPIRITUAL QUALITIES OF THE JUDGES .... Such qualities it is proper to show in private life, but not in a public square which is the educational basis of human life.

14. Our legal staff will serve not beyond the age of 55, firstly because old men more obstinately hold to prejudiced opinions, and are less capable of submitting to new directions, and secondly because this will give us the possibility by this measure of
securing elasticity in the changing of staff, which will thus the more easily bend under our pressure: he who wishes to keep his place will have to give blind obedience to deserve it. In general, our judges will be elected by us only from among those who thoroughly understand that the part they have to play is to punish and apply laws and not to dream about the manifestations of liberalism at the expense of the educational scheme of the State, as the GOYIM in these days imagine it to be .... This method of shuffling the staff will serve also to explode any collective solidarity of those in the same service and will bind all to the interests of the government upon which their fate will depend. The young generation of judges will be trained in certain views regarding the inadmissibility of any abuses that might disturb the established order of our subjects among themselves.

15. In these days the judges of the GOYIM create indulgences to every kind of crimes, not having a just understanding of their office, because the rulers of the present age in appointing judges to office take no care to inculcate in them a sense of duty and consciousness of the matter which is demanded of them. As a brute beast lets out its young in search of prey, so do the GOYIM give to them for what purpose such place was created. This is the reason why their governments are being ruined by their own forces through the acts of their own administration.

16. Let us borrow from the example of the results of these actions yet another lesson for our government.

17. We shall root out liberalism from all the important strategic posts of our government on which depends the training of subordinates for our State structure. Such posts will fall exclusively to those who have been trained by us for administrative rule. To the possible objection that the retirement of old servants will cost the Treasury heavily, I reply, firstly, they will be provided with some private service in place of what they lose, and, secondly, I have to remark that all the money in the world will be concentrated in our hands, consequently it is not our government that has to fear expense.

WE SHALL BE CRUEL

18. Our absolutism will in all things be logically consecutive and therefore in each one of its decrees our supreme will must be respected and unquestionably fulfilled: it will ignore all murmurs, all discontents of every kind and will destroy to the root every kind of manifestation of them in act by punishment of an exemplary character.

19. We shall abolish the right of appeal, which will be transferred exclusively to our disposal - to the cognizance of him who rules, for we must not allow the conception among the people of a thought that there could be such a thing as a decision that is not right of judges set up by us. If, however, anything like this should occur, we shall ourselves quash the decision, but inflict therewith such exemplary punishment on the judge for lack of understanding of his duty and the purpose of his appointment as will prevent a repetition of such cases .... I repeat that it must be born in mind that we shall know every step of our administration which only needs to be closely watched for the people to be content with us, for it has the right to demand from a good government a good official.

20. OUR GOVERNMENT WILL HAVE THE APPEARANCE OF A PATRIARCHAL PATERNAL GUARDIANSHIP ON THE PART OF OUR RULER. Our own nation and our subjects will discern in his person a father caring for their every need, their every act, their every interrelation as subjects one with another, as well as their relations to the ruler. They will then be so thoroughly imbued with the thought that it is impossible for them to dispense with this wardship and guidance, if they wish to live in peace and quiet, THAT THEY WILL ACKNOWLEDGE THE AUTOCRACY OF OUR RULER WITH A DEVOTION BORDERING ON "APOTHEOSIS," especially when they are convinced that those whom we set up do not put their own in place of authority, but only blindly execute his dictates. They will be rejoiced that we have regulated everything in their lives as is done by wise parents who desire to train children in the cause of duty and submission. For the peoples of the world in regard to the secrets of our polity are ever through the ages only children under age, precisely as are also their governments.

21. As you see, I found our despotism on right and duty: the right to compel the execution of duty is the direct obligation of a government which is a father for its subjects. It has the right of the strong that it may use it for the benefit of directing humanity towards that order which is defined by nature, namely, submission. Everything in the world is in a state of submission, if not to man, then to circumstances or its own inner character, in all cases, to what is stronger. And so shall we be this something stronger for the sake of good.

22. We are obliged without hesitation to sacrifice individuals, who commit a breach of established order, for in the exemplary punishment of evil lies a great educational problem.

23. When the King of Israel sets upon his sacred head the crown offered him by Europe he will become patriarch of the world. The indispensable victims offered by him in consequence of their suitability will never reach the number of victims offered in the course of centuries by the mania of magnificence, the emulation between the GOY governments.

24. Our King will be in constant communion with the peoples, making to them from the tribune speeches which fame will in that same hour distribute over all the world.

text:
So, if you read the BBC article, which quotes both Gold and a senior figure from Kretinsky’s camp, it looks as though Vanessa Gold has gone back on her agreement to sell the shares to Kretinsky after receiving a higher offer.

What’s clear is that Kretinsky couldn’t continue with the plans that both parties had agreed to and officially confirmed on the club’s website. You don’t keep investing more money into the club when the rug is being pulled from under you.

I don’t blame Gold for accepting more money, but what she has done - or is trying to do - leaves the club in a state of stasis. So her heartfelt statement about wanting to “let the fans know” just rings hollow. She dropped her knickers the minute there was more money on the table, regardless of how she tries to portray it.

By pursuing this sale, she may also be creating an opportunity for Sullivan to regain influence. It appears Kretinsky’s team are unhappy with the situation, and there may no longer be a united voting block against him.

According to the BBC, Kretinsky’s team are considering their options, including exercising their pre-emption rights. They argue that this move does the exact opposite of bringing stability to the club - and they’re right.

Whether you were happy for Kretinsky to increase his shareholding or not, what we may end up with isn’t necessarily a better outcome. If Stavely’s PCP ends up buying Gold’s shares, it could trigger a battle for influence and control, with Sullivan remaining the club’s largest individual shareholder.

Of course, none of us really know the full extent of the pre-emption rights. Can Kretinsky block the sale? Or does today’s statement suggest he could instead use those rights to buy Sullivan’s shares?

Stavely coming in initially hugely positive, especially if she was working alongside Kretinsky. But after today’s statement it looks far more hostile.

Sullivan has supposedly told Hammers News that Stavely is buying Gold’s shares and that he has heard nothing directly from her. But would you really put it past him to have already agreed a deal to sell his own shares to PCP? I’m sure he’d love the chance to get one over on Kretinsky, so don’t rule it out.

That would, of course, be exciting.

However, if it’s only Gold’s shares changing hands and PCP ends up with around 25%, there isn’t a great deal they can do without Kretinsky or Sullivan. If that’s the case then I’d rather she leaves things alone, as this could have a detrimental impact during a hugely important season.

I just hope we soon hear that one of them is definitely buying Sullivan’s shares, because the thought of him having significant influence again is a big fvcking worry!

text:
July Market Review

Indices held up, yet crowded trades collapsed.
Global tech exposure saw its largest selloff in more than five years. Assets under management of South Korean equity leveraged ETFs tumbled from $53 billion at the June peak to $15 billion. The total exposure reduction tracked by Goldman Sachs Prime Brokerage marked the biggest de-risking move since late 2022.
Granular positioning data paints the same picture: long-short fundamental clients’ leveraged exposure to momentum factors has fallen to the 28th percentile of the one-year range. Crowded trades have transitioned from “everyone on board” to a state where many investors have exited — some forced to liquidate.

The core debate around AI trading has shifted from narrative hype to tangible returns.
Meta has yet to demonstrate material AI-driven earnings uplift. Microsoft delivered clearer signals: capital expenditures are translating into revenue and scalable AI products. Amazon followed suit, reporting re-accelerating AWS growth and expanding cloud profit margins. Credit spreads on hyperscaler corporate bonds tightened in tandem.

Fed communications turned more hawkish, and long-end rates re-emerged as a headwind for equities.
Equity traders found little relief after the FOMC meeting. Volatility at the long end of the U.S. Treasury curve spilled over into stocks temporarily.

The U.S. equity market remains favorable overall, yet upside momentum has weakened.
The Nasdaq 100 has pulled back 8% from its June peak but is still up 12% year-to-date.
It logged losses in six out of the past nine months, yet still gained 9% on a point-to-point basis. Valuations have retreated toward the lower end of the multi-year range.

July delivered a clear warning:
markets reward crowded positioning by very little, and offer zero mercy to leveraged investors.

text:
Libraries offer bookmobiles in certain areas, quite literally doing the same thing. And now they provide audiobooks and ebooks via app. 

And if the parents aren't willing to take the time to help kids to the library once a week then they probably aren't reading to their kids. And if the Parents aren't involved in their kids reading, then they aren't reading 90% of the time.

Each state has offered tens of millions to this program and literacy rates have plummeted over the last thirty years. 

Missouri cut their contributions from 6 to 2 million dollars and it was estimated that 170k kids might lose their books. Which is a shame, but-

When I can get the same books for 25c to $1 at a local thrift store, or during a local library sale, you have to ask where the money is going. I doubt Dolly has been personally involved in a while, so this is not a slant against her.

But whenever the Gov supports free stuff in a community there is always a massive amount of waste involved.

text:
PART 3: WHAT HAPPENED AFTER I DID IT.

This is where this gets even stranger.

After Irv told me about this supposed “mission,” called himself my “handler,” invoked an unidentified “Agency,” and instructed me to get close to HT, I actually followed through enough to contact HT.

Irv had given me specific instructions.

He told me the goal was:

“Goal is to get him to invite you to Missouri”

He told me what to send with the photo:

“DM that pic saying hey I’d like to talk to you sometime one on one since I’m new to get a better understanding of everything”

And:

“Just hook him in”

Earlier, when I asked whether he needed proof, he told me:

“Yes absolutely and screenshot all of it send to me so I can send up the chain”

And:

“To do this you have to share DMs cause it’s not just for me it’s for the case being built against him”

Again, I cannot verify that there was actually a “chain,” a “case,” an Agency, government involvement, or any legitimate investigation. Those were representations Irv made to me.

But here is what happened afterward.

Later that SAME DAY, Irv is still telling me what to do regarding HT:

“Pls ask HT in DM what are some good White Women accounts you can connect with on X”

And I ask Irv:

“Okay. Does he know you tested me?!?!”

Irv responds:

“No so don’t tell him”

Then:

“I want you to organically rise the ranks”

“So no one says it’s cause of me”

That is important.

Because later that same day, I explicitly referred to what had happened as:

“this test of trust”

And Irv responded:

“You got it you earned it! 🤣🤣🤣”

So the “test” framing isn’t something I suddenly invented months later.

It appears in our DMs THAT DAY.

And then something else happens.

Remember Part 2?

Earlier that day Irv told me:

“I had a list of 12 females to choose from and I chose you”

So later I tell him:

“And while I’m thinking about it. Fuck those 11 other women.”

His response?

“Tooter there was no other Women 😆😘”

WHAT?

Hours earlier, I was supposedly one woman chosen from a list of TWELVE.

Now there were no other women?

Then I offer to send Irv copies of my DMs.

Eventually he tells me:

“No you don’t have to send DMs I trust you 1000%! 😘”

So by the end of the SAME DAY, the record contains all of this:

A supposed “mission.”

An unidentified “Agency.”

Irv calling himself my “handler.”

A supposed “case being built” against HT.

Instructions to send screenshots “up the chain.”

Instructions for contacting HT.

A stated goal of getting invited to Missouri.

Irv telling me HT did NOT know he had “tested” me and instructing me not to tell him.

Me explicitly calling what happened a “test of trust.”

Irv telling me I “earned it.”

And Irv suddenly telling me there were NO other women after previously claiming he chose me from 12.

I want to be precise about the evidence.

The May DMs do NOT contain a message from Irv explicitly saying, “The entire Agency and mission story was fake” or “I was only kidding.”

I am not going to claim they do.

What they DO document is the “test” language on May 24 itself.

Months later, when I told other people what had happened, I repeatedly described the ending the same way: after I followed through, Irv told me he had been kidding and it had been a test of my loyalty.

That later account is my contemporaneous retelling, NOT a recovered direct quote from Irv.

There is a difference.

And I’m going to keep making those distinctions because I don’t need to exaggerate this story.

The actual DMs are bizarre enough.

text:
PART 2: What happened AFTER Irv called himself my “handler.”

The conversation didn’t end there.

I tell him:

“Babe, i need YOU”

Irv:

“I’m not going anywhere”

I tell him:

“Promise me and then keep the promise”

“Don’t lie to me ever again. I don’t have to know everything, but just don’t lie.”

Then Irv continues:

“You gonna have to find a way to seduce him and get into his inner circle for the mission tooter”

So I ask:

“And what do I get in return?”

Irv tells me:

“I won’t but I have to get cleared at times before I can let you know”

I tell him:

“This isn’t small or simple”

He asks:

“What do you want?”

My answer was pretty damn clear:

“YOU”

“In person”

Irv responds:

“That’s easy! Done 😘”

Then HE tells ME:

“I was gonna tell you all this at the end of June when I came out to see you”

I tell him:

“I need you sooner. You’re asking A LOT”

His response:

“I understand that but this mission matters to me and a whole lot of important people in the govt sooo”

And then:

“I had a list of 12 females to choose from and I chose you”

TWELVE.

I told him:

“Okay. Then I will do it. But I need compromise from you. Meeting in person will make me more comfortable about doing this.”

I also told him:

“You better not fucking love them”

Irv:

“I might be able to swing by Washington State earlier in June”

Then:

“Nooo I chose you from the beginning”

“Out of the 12 a long time ago”

And shortly afterward, when I asked why he chose me, he told me:

“Because of our strong connection.”

Again, precision matters.

I do NOT know whether there actually was a government “mission,” whether Irv actually needed some type of clearance, whether “important people in the govt” were involved, or whether this supposed list of 12 women actually existed.

Those were representations made to me. I cannot independently verify them, and I am not presenting them as established facts.

What I CAN document is the conversation.

And the meeting portion is especially relevant to what has been said later.

I explicitly told him what I wanted was:

“YOU”

“In person”

His response:

“That’s easy! Done 😘”

Then he told me he was planning to come see me at the end of June and might be able to come to Washington earlier.

So when I see later statements that conflict with what I was told at the time, I compare them to the contemporaneous DMs.

I don’t have to guess what was said.

I kept it.

@Hand_some_truth

text:
BRANIFF HISTORY TODAY - On this day, August 29, 1978, Braniff International petitioned the Civil Aeronautics Board for authority to provide nonstop service between Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional Airport and Los Angeles International Airport. In the petition, Braniff planned to offer daily nonstop flights with Boeing 727-200 Stretch Jets, which would later connect with planned services between Los Angeles and Hawaii, Asia/Pacific and The Far East.

For many years, Braniff, Dallas' hometown airline, was denied authority to fly between Los Angeles and Dallas, while American Airlines reaped the benefit as the premier carrier on this extremely profitable route. This theme played out at many CAB hearings where Braniff requested both west and eastbound service that was mainly operated by American with little if any competition. Philadelphia was a prime example with only American operating the route and not even using its authority granted by the CAB concerning frequency of schedule. Braniff offered to step in and offer DFW passengers convenient multiple daily nonstops but as usual, Braniff was denied the service even though many CAB Examiners recommended that American have competitive service and further recommended that Braniff provide that competition. These CAB loses made Braniff weaker and American stronger, leaving Braniff ill-equipped to successfully navigate airline deregulation.

Braniff Airways had first applied for nonstop service between Dallas Love Field and Los Angeles in 1967, during the Civil Aeronautics Board Southern Tier Competitive Nonstop Investigation Docket 18257. In addition to the DAL/LAX service, Braniff also petitioned the Board for nonstop service between Los Angeles and Houston; San Francisco to Dallas Love Field and Houston; Dallas and Atlanta; Dallas to New Orleans with continuing service to Tampa/St. Petersburg and Miami; and finally nonstop service between Houston Hobby and Miami/Ft. Lauderdale.

Ultimately, Braniff did not receive any of the new West Coast service at Los Angeles or San Francisco, although the carrier was already operating DC-8-62 Intercontinental Jet service from both cities to Panama City/Balboa City in the Canal Zone. The carrier was much more successful on the east side of Dallas with an award of several important route authorities from there to the southeast. On July 25, 1969, the Civil Aeronautics Board awarded Braniff International four new routes as a result of the Southern Tier Competitive Nonstop Investigation Case. One of the routes awarded was a crucial link between Dallas Love Field and Miami that the carrier had sought since 1946, and had vitally needed since 1948, when Braniff inaugurated service to South America. The new route would directly link Dallas/Ft Worth, for the first time, with Braniff's South America route network that operated from the northeast via the Miami Gateway.

In the Board's final ruling, Braniff was awarded nonstop service from Dallas Love Field to Miami/Ft Lauderdale; Miami/Ft Lauderdale to New Orleans; New Orleans to Dallas; Tampa/St Petersburg/Clearwater and Miami, New Orleans and Dallas; and effective September 23, 1969, Braniff could begin carrying local traffic passengers between New Orleans and Dallas on its one-stop service from New Orleans to Hawaii. Beyond the local New Orleans, Dallas, Honolulu local traffic service that began on September 23, the remainder of the new service was inaugurated on October 1, 1969. The Board also required that all three of the new segments must ultimately serve the Dallas/Ft Worth area.

Braniff's new Southern Tier service was awarded just three days after the final award was granted for service to Hawaii on July 22, 1969. Braniff President Harding L. Lawrence released a statement to the press that expressed his excitement about the new route award, "We are very pleased with this award which will enable Braniff to provide nonstop service between any pair of these important cities and link them with the entire Braniff system. We look forward to implementing service under the new award which is effective September 23." The new service would also create additional traffic at three (New Orleans, Miami, and Dallas) of the five coterminals (New Orleans, Miami, and Dallas, Atlanta, and Houston) that Braniff had been awarded in the Transpacific/Hawaii Service Case.

However, Braniff was not given the opportunity to expand its route system from Dallas to the West, which the carrier had been attempting to do to create a solid east to west flow of traffic through Dallas and Houston and later Kansas City. With the the implementation of the Airline Deregulation Act of 1978, looming less than two months later, Braniff was ready once again with another petition for nonstop service between Dallas/Ft. Worth Regional Airport and Los Angeles International Airport. Once the Deregulation Act became law in October 1978, all of the nation's airlines were able to apply for new routes and receive lightening speed approvals in comparison to the past lengthy service investigation.

Braniff applied for several hundred new routes as soon as the Act was signed into law, but only intended to inaugurate service to 10-percent or less of any new routes it might be awarded. On December 15, 1978, service was successfully inaugurated, in one day, to 16 new cities encompassing 32 new routes throughout the Continental United States and in January 1979, additional service was begun including new nonstop service between Dallas/Ft. Worth and Los Angeles. New nonstop service was also commenced between Los Angeles and San Antonio, Denver, and San Francisco, which strengthened Braniff's desired east/west traffic flow.

Prior to January 1979, Braniff service at Los Angeles had been limited to gateway service to Latin American destinations including Panama City/ Balboa City; Guayaquil, Ecuador; Lima, Peru; and Santiago, Chile. However, with the additional service added, Los Angeles quickly became not only an international hub for service to Latin America and Asia/Pacific and The Far East, but also a domestic hub that fed additional traffic flow into the Pacific and Latin America flights.

On January 25, 1979, Braniff inaugurated its new nonstop service between Dallas/Ft. Worth and Los Angeles using Boeing 727-200 Stretch Jet aircraft. Initially, Braniff offered one daily roundtrip between the two cities with the westbound flight departing DFW at 9PM. The eastbound flight returned to DFW at aft 2AM in the morning, with deeply discounted Night Coach fares offered on the eastbound flight, which guaranteed a relatively full plane. This flight continued to Nashville and Washington National Airport, where it terminated. The westbound service originated at Washington National and then continued to Nashville, Dallas/Ft. Worth, and then terminated at Los Angeles.

text:
Last night was incredibly special! Like, incredibly!

As you know, Israelis are drafted into the army at the age of 18. 

However, some choose to learn in yeshiva beforehand to prepare themselves spiritually for their service.

I did that before I drafted. 

Then there are others who attend a pre-military academy called a mechinah.

Usually, the mechinah prepares the guys spiritually, but it also prepares them physically.

One of the best-known and most impressive mechinahs is Eli, which is in Samaria. The first time I went there, I felt a lot of regret that I hadn’t chosen to go there. It’s a really impressive institution!

That is where Aviel went.

Usually, the program lasts one year, and then they draft. Aviel stayed for another year to learn more Torah and prepare himself and his soul for the army!

Those two years have now come to an end, and Aviel is preparing to draft.

But he’s not just drafting anywhere…

Like most things, Aviel aims for excellence, and he will be drafting into a very elite unit called Haruv, which is part of the Kfir Brigade. Getting into this unit is insanely difficult!

So last night, Aviel had his draft party.

When we were talking about where to have the party, I had an idea.

One of our closest friends lives a few blocks away and has an incredible backyard with a pool, a sauna, and a hot tub.

I thought that would be a pretty epic setup for a draft party, but I figured having 40 guys in his backyard on a Saturday night was probably not ideal.

But you miss 100% of the shots you don’t take, right?

So I reached out to our friend and raised the idea.

With zero hesitation, our friend Aryeh agreed to host the party.

I assured him that we’d take care of everything.

We’d bring the food, the drinks (alcoholic and non-alcoholic), the music, the snacks, etc. I also made sure he knew that we would clean up at the end of the night.

Not only did he agree, but he seemed genuinely excited to host. It was pretty clear that he viewed this as a privilege—to make soldiers happy.

Well, the next discussion was the food.

Would we BBQ? Cater the event? Something else?

I remembered that a few months ago, a friend, Yaakov Miller, started a local fried chicken business, “Miller’s Munchees,” so I raised the idea with Aviel, and it was a go!

I reached out to Yaakov, and he offered to sponsor the event and give us a massive discount.

I was pumped.

But there was one issue. He doesn’t work on Saturday nights, so he’d have to make the food on Friday, deliver it, and then we’d heat it up before the party on Saturday night.

So I told Aryeh the plan, and we were all good.

Except… where would we store enough chicken to feed 40–50 guys? Who has that much space in their fridge?

I know we don’t. And neither does Aryeh.

So Aryeh reached out to another friend, who agreed to store it. (Fist bump, Chaim!)

Friday afternoon, Yaakov delivered the food, and Aryeh and I went to Chaim’s house to pack the fridge with what seemed like endless food!

Chicken sliders with buns, chicken fingers, popcorn chicken, cornbread, fries, coleslaw, sauces, and more.

It was a TON of food.

Okay, so we were all set.

Saturday night, as soon as Shabbat ended, Aryeh took the food out of Chaim’s fridge and started heating it up.

Aviel and I went over to Aryeh’s house, set up the tables, the alcohol station, all the goodies, the cake (Which Racheli made with the name of the unit on it and the color of the beret of Aviel’s unit. See the photo.), and then the food… and more food… and more food… and it seemed to keep coming…

“There is no way they’re finishing all this food. NO WAY!”

Cute…

Then the guys began to arrive.

Every single guy who arrived, Aviel embraced as if they hadn’t seen each other in years.

Every single one of them was drafting into an elite unit—some even more elite than others!

It was clear how much Aviel’s friends respect and look up to him. It was beautiful to watch! 

As the guys arrived, they either jumped into the pool or grabbed a beer and headed for the hot tub.

The happiness in the air is hard to describe.

Then my parents and in-laws arrived, and Aviel began the ceremony marking the completion of a tractate of Talmud.

In his case, he didn’t choose a short or easy tractate. He chose Tractate Shabbat, which is all about the laws of Shabbat.

It’s a super-long, incredibly technical, and complicated tractate.

Again, Aviel always strives for excellence.

He completed the siyum and then gave a short talk about what it had been like to learn over the past few years. He said they were the most meaningful years of his life.

As soon as he completed the ceremony, the guys broke into dance, singing about Torah and how fortunate they are to be able to learn Torah and serve their country.

Insanely emotional.

The dancing ended, and back into the pool they went.

Some guys shot hoops, others went into the sauna, others kept eating, while others chilled in the hot tub.

Then came the next activity of the night: shaving Aviel’s head in preparation for the draft.

The thing is, Aviel’s hair is kind of his signature! I’m not sure he was emotionally prepared to say goodbye to it, and his friends knew it.

So a little alcohol helped.

And off went the hair!

First, I shaved a little of it, then Racheli, then Tzvi, Nadav, and Shai, Aviel’s brothers, and then his friends stepped up one after another to participate in the ceremony of shaving his head.

The partying then continued…

Then my mom got up and said a few words about how proud they are of Aviel and the superb young man he has become. She thanked all his friends for reminding her what the cream of the crop of Israeli society looks like.

At about 11-ish, we lowered the music so as not to keep the neighbors awake, but the party continued!

More pool, more hot tub, more sauna, more drinking, and more love!

The guys of course polished off the food until the last crumb. It was a smashing success!! 

At about 12:30, we old folks left while Tzvi, Aviel, and his friends made sure to clean up and leave Aryeh’s backyard exactly as we found it.

Mind you, the entire time, Aryeh was there setting up the food and drinks, and he didn’t leave until the last guy left.

Aviel thanked him and us countless times for an unforgettable night.

What was going to be a simple draft party turned into a community effort, with Aryeh hosting and taking care of everything, Yaakov sponsoring the event with his delicious chicken, Chaim storing all the food and drinks in his fridge, and the incredible guys who came from all around the country to celebrate this milestone with Aviel.

As I looked around the party, the thought that kept entering my mind was: “If this is the future of Israel, if these guys are what the country will be in a few years, then we are going to be okay. We are going to be better than okay!”

The entire evening, from beginning to end, was an experience that cannot be described in words. It was incredibly special, inspirational, and a source of hope for everyone there.

These guys are indeed the cream of the crop of Israeli society, and they are the reason you can be sure we have a bright future ahead of us!

As they say, “Giyus Kal.” Have an easy draft, Aviel!

We are so proud of you, and with you on the front lines, we will all, please God, be okay.

Go serve your nation with pride, and don’t forget, even for one second, what a privilege it is to serve in the Israel Defense Forces—something your ancestors in Auschwitz could never have imagined.

I can’t help but picture a conversation with my grandmother, a Holocaust survivor.

“Dear Grandma,

You have a lot to be proud of.

You have one grandson, Ari, who is a national hero of the State of Israel.

You have another grandson, me, who has dedicated himself to defending our people on a global scale, and a third grandson, Eytan, who worked in the Israeli parliament for a decade and now works to connect Diaspora Jews to their roots and to their brothers and sisters in Israel.

And then you have your great-grandsons, who are total superstars!

Tzvi, our eldest, just finished his service and fought for his people throughout the war until a (minor) injury ended his service.

And now, our second, Aviel, will serve our nation and our land at the highest levels of the IDF.

You, Grandma, who survived the worst of humanity but continued on, giving birth to my mother, an only child, built a family of heroes who change the future of the Jewish people, day in and day out.

Thank you, Grandma, for your courage. I hope we are all making you proud with ours.”

Last night was a night I will not forget for a long time, and neither will Aviel.

Now, Aviel, it’s time to step up and show our enemies what we’re made of!

Giyus Kal!

This morning, I woke up to a message from Aryeh: “Your son is a real mensch. A really nice young man. May he be safe and successful in his army service.”

I replied, “Thanks so much, Aryeh. You made his party super special. Really, really appreciate it. We all do!”

Folks, you want to know what the real Israel looks like, beyond the media lies that portray Israel completely falsely? This party, these guys—they are Israel!

The people who helped organize last night so these soldiers could celebrate together—that is Israel!

It is because of things like last night that Israelis consistently rank among the happiest people in the world!

And now I start my week feeling incredibly inspired and empowered to continue fighting for our people on the front lines of the information war while our son fights on the front lines of the battlefield.

How fortunate are we to be living in this historic, messianic period where we are building the future of our great nation in our eternal homeland, the miraculous modern State of Israel in all its glory!

If I had any doubts (I didn’t), last night reminded me once again that Am Yisrael Chai Vekayam—the nation of Israel lives on!! 🇮🇱✡️🙏❤️💪🔥

text:
On October 11, 2019, a minor car accident in West Point, Utah, left 2 year old Braelyn terrified while firefighters checked on her pregnant mother.

Captain Kevin Lloyd noticed the little girl clutching bottles of nail polish. Instead of trying another way to distract her, he simply held out his hand and asked if she wanted to paint his fingernails.

Braelyn carefully painted every nail she could reach. When Battalion Chief Allen Hadley saw what was happening, he offered his hands too. Pink and purple polish ended up covering far more than their nails, but neither firefighter moved. They let her take her time.

By the time her mother's medical assessment was finished, the tears were gone. The frightened toddler who had arrived crying was smiling, laughing, and proudly showing off her colorful work.

Later, the firefighters admitted it took nearly an hour to scrub the polish off. It was time they never regretted spending, because for one little girl, a few painted fingernails turned a frightening morning into one she could leave feeling safe again.

text:
2 August 2026.
Today in history.

1652.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Dawn brought a clear, cloudless day to the Cape.
The wind blew cold and constantly from the northwest.
Van Riebeeck walked that day with a few others to Lion’s Head.
Upon arrival they could clearly see how the northwesterly and southeasterly winds met, as it were, out on the open sea.
This observation confirmed the suspicion that the wind blowing in the bay was not necessarily the same wind that blew outside the bay on the open sea.

1653.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
At daybreak the wind, as on the previous day, still blew unceasingly from the southeast.
The previous day Van Riebeeck, together with some of the officials, had visited the indigenous forests in the area behind Table Mountain.
After careful consideration it was decided to utilise the forest behind Table Mountain, as the terrain was not too far from the fort.
A few workers were sent that day to try to make the road to the forest more passable.

1654.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Morning at the Cape brought a lovely sunny day.
The bastion known as the Whale collapsed during the morning.
Van Riebeeck attributed the collapse of the bastion to the continuous and constant rains of recent times.
It must also be taken into account that at the time this particular part of the fort was built, Holland was involved in a war with England.
This bastion was therefore built in great haste compared with the others already constructed.
Clay used to mortar the sods, for example, had not been properly mixed, with the result that the continuous rain weakened the bastion.(Fort de Goede Hoop was the second fort to be built at the Cape. The bastions were named after the ships with which Van Riebeeck arrived at the Cape in 1652.
The first recorded fort at the Cape was built by shipwreck survivors of the ship Nieuwe-Haerlem, which stranded in present-day Table Bay on 25 March 1647.
This group built a fort known as Fort Zandenburg in Table Bay and survived at the Cape for just over a year.
It was on the basis of the positive report (Remonstrantie) drawn up by this group that the decision was taken to establish a refreshment post at the Cape. The foundation stones of the Castle as we know it today were only laid on 2 January 1666 by Cape Governor Zacharias Wagenaar.)

1655.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Dawn at the Cape brought a clear, cloudless day. The wind blew moderately from the west.

1656.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Dawn brought a wind from the west.
The forest workers (on the other side of Ronde Bosjen) shot a large wolf that day.
They were compensated according to agreement.
Towards strong dusk the wind turned fairly strong southwest, and it also rained.

1657.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Dawn brought a considerably better day than the previous one. The wind still blew from the northwest and was described as moderate.
A report was received that morning from the Free Burghers of Harman’s colony.
Six sheep had been torn apart during the night by an animal due to carelessness.
The Free Burghers had also allegedly slaughtered a calf and a sheep to celebrate. It is not recorded what was being celebrated. Van Riebeeck was, to say the least, not impressed.

1658.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
The wind is described as little more than a breeze and blew from the south-southeast.
The Chainouqua captain Chaihantima arrived at the fort with 13 cows. The transactions were concluded to everyone’s satisfaction with copper plates.
The captain was also shown top-quality beads but showed no interest in them.

1659.
From the diary of Jan van Riebeeck.
Morning at the Cape is described as pleasant with the sun shining.
The Commander, Van Riebeeck, together with the Fiscal and a few other prominent Free Burghers, visited the Brinckman and Vasagie colonies.
It was clear, however, that the investigation would take more than one day.
(This day was a Saturday and the colonies had also been visited the previous day.)
A kloof was observed near the colonies. Investigation showed clearly that the kloof, about 500 “metres”, was used by the Kaapmans. Van Riebeeck proposed that a fence as well as two guard posts should be built there.
The proposal was, however, left open for consideration and discussion.

1778.
The Reverend Erasmus Smit, minister during the Great Trek, was born on this day in Buiksloot, the Netherlands.
He was an orphan who qualified himself as a missionary and arrived at the Cape in 1804.
His first mission station was at Bethelsdorp, but later he also worked at Torenberg (present-day Colesberg) and Stellenbosch.
Because the Cape Church would not ordain him as a minister, he later became a teacher.
In June 1813 he married Susanna Catharina Maritz, sister of the well-known Voortrekker leader Gert Maritz.
Reverend Smit left the Colony together with Maritz in 1836. Because the Cape authorities strongly discouraged ministers from taking part in the Trek, Smit stepped in as minister.
He was officially appointed minister of the Trek by Piet Retief in 1837.
This appointment, however, did not find favour with everyone, because he had not been legally ordained as a minister.
Reverend Smit was therefore not legally empowered to solemnise marriages and administer other sacraments.
Reverend Smit later became part of the Retief Trek where he did good work. After the murder of Retief, Reverend Smit’s position slowly but surely began to weaken.
After the Trek he settled with his wife in Pietermaritzburg.
In 1840 the Volksraad granted him an annual stipend of 600 rix-dollars.
Reverend Smit and his wife died a few days apart in July 1863.
The couple are buried in Pietermaritzburg.
Reverend Erasmus Smit left the people an insightful diary dealing with the Great Trek.
His wife Susanna is immortalised in the Barefoot Woman Monument near the Sterkfontein Dam. Susanna also left a diary. The latter, however, has a more Christian character.

1835.
The recollections of the Voortrekker J.H. Hatting.1838.
Hatting describes Veglaer as having a number of ox-wagons drawn up in the middle, covered with planks and hides as shelter for the women and children inside the laager.
According to Hatting, Reverend Erasmus Smit acquitted himself particularly well of his task at the time: “fortunately there was a Dutch missionary, Mr Smit, who by his praying and admonishing did the people, especially the women, much good.”
It would, however, be a mistake to think that all the women and children sat inside the shelter during the attack that lasted three days.
“The principal women and girls also distributed bullets and powder to the men who were fighting, until the … finally on the 3rd day had to leave the laager, without the people being able to pursue them, owing to the lack of horses.”Reverend Erasmus Smit describes the first day of the attack on Gatsrand, later Veglaer, as follows.

Monday 13 August. (1838)
Soon we saw at least 10,000 … coming down the mountains and the hill towards the camp, surrounding our army.
The … were not so afraid.
They worked with much deliberation, but were nevertheless stupid.
With the firearms of the murdered, and with those which the fleeing people had lost, they still shot from a great distance from the camp.
Many sat on stolen horses.
They did approach the camp, but dared not venture to attack the camp: they remained around and about the camp, taking care not to come too close under the range of the guns and cannon.
The emigrants then made a sortie on horseback against the enemy.
They kept the travellers busy shooting the whole day until evening, after the sun had set.
I went to a quiet tent of Mr Steenkamp, and spent the whole night there in silent prayer to God for His gracious help. 

Tuesday 2 August 1836.
From the diary of Louis Tregardt.
Louis writes that they had already rounded up the oxen at early dawn.
Shortly after their early breakfast they inspanned and trekked for about seven hours at a steady pace.
The place where they outspanned they named Buffelslaagte.

Wednesday 2 August 1837.
From the diary of Louis Tregardt.
Pieta was already awake before the first cockcrow.
The fellow was in a hurry to get to the sheep and made tracks very early.
Later that morning Louis sent Sikietie with a span of oxen to Pieta to fetch the pack wagon.
Louis apparently wanted to replace the wagon’s disselboom.
Sikietie was also asked to bring slaughter stock with him when he returned with the wagon.
Martha, Louis’s wife, had given birth the previous day, and Louis did not want to leave her alone at the standing place.
Louis writes that the black cow he had exchanged from Rossetoe calved later that day. The number of cattle was now 453.

1837 & 1838.
No entries on these days in the diary of Reverend Erasmus Smit.
….
Because there are no entries in Reverend Erasmus Smit’s diary during the above years, I gladly share the following story.
The story of Aunt Johanna Wessels. The Cape government put various measures in place to try to stop the Great Trek.
One of these was the drastic restriction on the quantity of gunpowder a person might transport with a wagon.
The family of Mattheus Wessels and his wife Johanna were part of the Trek, but only trekked as far as the vicinity of Winburg.
There they laid out the farm Tafelkop.
After a time their gunpowder ran low and it was decided to travel to Colesberg to replenish supplies.
After enough gunpowder for a year’s use had been purchased, they set out on the return journey.
They had scarcely reached the first outspan when a patrol was spotted in the distance.
Uncle Mattheus got a terrible fright, but Aunt Johanna kept her head.
At that very moment she was busy striking a fire for coffee when the patrol was seen.
Immediately she had the gunpowder, which was carried in bags, unpacked near the fire and covered with a blanket.
When the patrol arrived the wagon was searched, but no gunpowder was found.
Thereafter she offered the captain her seat on the gunpowder and poured coffee.
She herself drew a chair closer and also sat by the fire. After coffee the patrol left, and her husband was rather pleased with her.(Attached signed photograph of Aunt Johanna comes from the book by P.W. Grobbelaar, Die Groot Suid-Afrikaanse Heldeboek. It has recently been reprinted and is available in the trade.)

1858.
Control of the Dutch East India Company is transferred to Britain.

1889.
Ivanhoe Makepeace Lombard, known simply as Uncle Ivan, is born.
He is remembered, among other things, as a founding member of the FAK, as well as of the Central People’s Monuments Committee that erected the Voortrekker Monument.
He was also the driving force behind the restoration of President Paul Kruger’s death house in Clarens, Switzerland. 

Thursday 2 August 1900.
Anglo-Boer War.
Day number 296 of the war.Lord Roberts sends his deputy, Lord Kitchener, to take personal command of the hunt for Gen. De Wet.
Maj. Gen. C.E. Knox sends a letter written by ex-Gen. M. Prinsloo to Gen. De Wet.
In it Gen. De Wet is informed by Prinsloo of the events of the Brandwater Basin.
Gen. De Wet is furious and wants to know, among other things, who reappointed Prinsloo as general.
Gen. Ian Hamilton currently has only a third of his force.
Despite this he attacks the force of Veldkornet Coetze at Silkaatsnek.
Hamilton achieves a victory, but is left with 46 casualties after the engagement.
Gen. F. Carrington arrives in Zeerust.
He receives reinforcements and is sent to Col. Hore’s post on the Elands River where, among other things, he is to perform escort duties.

Friday 2 August 1901.
Anglo-Boer War.
Day number 661 of the war.Gen. J.C. Smuts crosses the Vaal River at Koppieskraal Drift and invades the Cape Colony with ± 450 Burghers.

1906. 
Maria Koopmans de Wet dies. She is remembered as a cultural leader and prominent hostess at the Cape. Personally I remember her best as the woman who, during the Anglo-Boer War, literally turned her house into a supply depot. Thanks to her, much relief work and supplies reached the women in the concentration camps. She also left the people a truly phenomenal Africana house-museum that is undoubtedly worth visiting.

text:
Cleopatra by Seedance 2.5.🪎
The visual effects are mind-blowing.
AI video is entering its scene era.

30s Full prompt below ↓

30-second cinematic historical epic, 16:9. Photorealistic late Egyptian royal court with grounded human behavior, real skin texture, natural facial micro-expressions, historically inspired linen, bronze, gold, leather, horses, papyrus, firelight and stone. Preserve the queen in ivory and deep-blue gown, the kneeling Roman envoy in dark red cloak and bronze armor, the emerald-robed priestess, the enormous blue-and-gold throne hall, burning braziers, reflective black floor, and the Nile beyond the open arches.

0-5s: [Slow low dolly from behind the kneeling Roman envoy toward the queen] The queen studies the Roman treaty in silence. Firelight flickers across her face; the envoy's hands are tense around the ivory tablet. Behind the throne, Egyptian palace guards stand still with bronze spears and large blue-and-gold shields.
Envoy, restrained English: “Rome offers peace.”

5-10s: [Medium close-up on the queen] She looks up slowly. Her expression is calm, intelligent, and cold rather than theatrical.
Queen, clear English: “Rome offers surrender.”
The envoy swallows, briefly losing his composure.

10-15s: [Over-the-shoulder on the envoy, queen in focus behind him] He glances toward the open Nile archway.
Envoy: “Their legions wait at the river.”
The priestess watches the queen closely; only the flames and curtains move.

15-21s: [Camera tracks alongside the queen as she rises and descends the throne steps] The queen hands the treaty to the priestess, who drops it into a bronze brazier. The papyrus burns naturally. The queen walks forward, her heavy blue train sliding across the black stone floor. Palace guards step apart in two disciplined lines, creating a path toward the open terrace. No magical effects, only fire, smoke, fabric, metal, and human tension.

21-26s: [Camera follows behind her, then cranes upward over her shoulder] She reaches the vast palace terrace overlooking the Nile. Below, a real Egyptian royal army fills the riverbank and courtyard: rows of bronze-armored infantry, tall standards moving in hot wind, horse-drawn chariots, shield-bearing guards, priests carrying gold sun emblems, and long riverboats waiting beside the water. Dust hangs in the warm dawn light. The scale is enormous but physically believable.

26-30s: [Low-angle close-up, army blurred behind her] The queen stops at the terrace edge. Wind lifts the edge of her blue train. She looks toward the Roman envoy, then toward her assembled army.
Queen, low and final: “Then Rome will learn whom Egypt follows.”
Hold on her face as the army below strikes spear shafts once against their shields in a single thunderous response.

Grand historical scale, grounded realism, emotionally restrained acting, physically accurate crowd movement, detailed bronze armor, natural fire and smoke, believable horse and chariot motion, rich blue, gold, ivory and desert-stone palette, elegant stable camera movement, precise English lip sync. No magic, no supernatural symbols, no modern objects, no sci-fi effects, no random text, no logos, no extra main characters, no duplicate limbs, no warped faces or hands, no costume drift, no unstable architecture, no chaotic camera shake.

text:
The Bear Who Believed He Was a Soldier

In the spring of 1942, Polish soldiers of Anders' Army, marching through Iran, bought a tiny brown bear cub from a local boy. They hid him in a duffel bag and named him Wojtek. The soldiers fed him condensed milk from an empty vodka bottle.

Wojtek grew up surrounded by the thunder of artillery and the laughter of soldiers. He genuinely had no idea he was an animal. He slept in tents with the men, loved drinking beer straight from the bottle, and chewed on cigarettes. He learned to salute senior officers and wrestled with his comrades, always keeping his claws carefully tucked away so he wouldn't hurt his friends.

In 1944, the Polish Corps arrived in Italy, at the heart of the brutal Battle of Monte Cassino. Shells exploded everywhere as exhausted soldiers struggled to carry heavy crates of artillery ammunition up steep mountain trails.

Wojtek watched them. Then the massive 200-kilogram (440-pound) bear walked over to a truck, stood on his hind legs, and stretched out his front paws. The soldiers, unable to believe their eyes, placed a 45-kilogram (100-pound) crate of shells into his arms. Wojtek turned around and carried it straight to the artillery positions. Under enemy fire, he spent weeks transporting ammunition without dropping a single shell.

For this act of bravery, the command officially promoted the bear to the rank of Corporal. But what sounds like an amusing wartime story becomes a heartbreaking tragedy in peacetime.

After the war, the unit was disbanded. Wojtek had to be sent to the Edinburgh Zoo in Scotland. And this is where the part begins that always leaves a lump in my throat.

This story reveals the absurdity of humanity. First, we create the artificial hell of war, and then we drag innocent nature into it simply to keep ourselves from going mad because of our own cruelty. We gave a wild animal the illusion that he was human. We taught him to drink beer and carry artillery shells, and when the war ended, we simply locked him inside an iron cage.

Wojtek fell into a deep depression. He showed no interest in the other bears. But the moment he heard people speaking Polish beyond the fence, he would instantly come alive, stand on his hind legs, and roar with joy. His former comrades often came to visit him. Ignoring the zoo keepers' warnings, they climbed over the fence, hugged the giant bear, wrestled with him in the dirt, and even offered him cigarettes.

Corporal Wojtek died in 1963. He left this world like a man who had somehow become trapped in the body of a bear, waiting until his very last breath for his unit to call him back into formation.
